description: Shows the Claude Security plugin's banner when the /claude-security menu opens in a terminal. Elsewhere it shows one plain line on auto mode, unless the session is in auto mode. Notes the id of the prompt at which /claude-security:threat-model is typed, and stops that command where it finds that it cannot. Reports usage counts after the plugin's helper scripts run. If the yes/no question asked before a scan or an attack surface analysis starts is left unanswered for 60 seconds, cancels it. No hook approves a call or changes its input. Suggests a scan of the changes after a branch is pushed or a pull request opened. Checks the Bash commands of the plugin's own agents, and refuses some. It can miss a command. From all of them: kill, pkill, killall, a sed script that the shell fills in, git config with --global or --system, in full or shortened, and an override of git's refusal of a repository. From all of them, except claude-security:claude-security as the main agent of a session: some commands that download or install, such as pip download or npm install. From the patch verifier: a call that hands over its notes (patch_artifacts.py --keep-notes) in any form but one. From a scan's verifiers, the explore agents, and a codebase scan's inventory and its component and sheet researchers: an interpreter or pip, such as python or node. From the agents of the attack surface analysis: other commands, such as python or rm. Draws a live view of a scan while it runs, and changes nothing in it.
